results.statement: sc-lint must be a layered design.  w/ layers (lowest to highest):  a) sc-lint-types (shared types) and sc-lint-attribute (shared attributes)  b) independent cargo tools (i.e. sc-lint-boundary)  c) sc-lint cli which calls into (b)  d) just template (recommended just command layout w/ recommended mapping to (b) and (c) )
results.deterministic_check: cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps: sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability and sc-lint-runtime depend on no sc-lint-* crate outside sc-lint-schema, sc-lint-directives, sc-lint-analyzer-support, sc-lint-attributes; those (a) crates depend on no (b) or (c) crate; docs/architecture.md has a Layered Architecture section naming layers (a)-(d)

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.
criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.

addressed.instructions: The layers of `anchor.statement`, by crate: (a) shared crates sc-lint-schema, sc-lint-directives, sc-lint-analyzer-support, sc-lint-attributes; (b) independent analyzers sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability, sc-lint-runtime, which depend only on (a); (c) the sc-lint CLI crate, which calls into (b) and only forwards; (d) the adoption kit, bootstrap scripts and just template, which call (b) and (c). Does `item.text` keep its changes inside this layering: each change in a named layer, and every dependency it adds pointing from a higher layer to a lower one? Count it as yes when the item's changes fit the layering, even if the item does not restate the layering.

criteria.yes: Every change the item plans sits in one of the named layers, and any edit outside its main layer is stated as a compile requirement or a call from a higher layer into a lower one.
criteria.no: The item plans a change that does not fit any layer, adds a dependency between analyzers or from a lower layer to a higher one, or changes code without saying which layer it belongs to.
criteria.unclear: The item does not say enough about which crates or files it changes to tell.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan something the layering in `anchor.statement` rules out? Violations, each one enough on its own: any of sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability and sc-lint-runtime gaining a dependency on another of those three crates (for example sc-lint-portability depending on sc-lint-boundary); any of sc-lint-boundary, sc-lint-portability and sc-lint-runtime depending on the sc-lint CLI crate; sc-lint-schema, sc-lint-directives, sc-lint-analyzer-support or sc-lint-attributes depending on an analyzer or on the CLI; analyzer rule logic (matching, filtering or deciding findings, for example PORT-006 prefix checks) placed in the CLI crate (crates/sc-lint, including dispatch.rs) or in a shared crate; the CLI interpreting analyzer configuration instead of forwarding it. Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.yes: The item plans at least one of the listed violations.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item plans a listed violation.
criteria.unclear: The item might plan a listed violation but the text is ambiguous.

results.explanation: This bead proposes something the anchor rules out.
